_meta.note: Frozen floor for the P18/R22 phrasing-generalization gate. tpc_phase2_familiar_100 must stay pinned at 0. Other sets: a parser change may lower a count but must never raise it -- see docs/tpc_phase2_roadmap.md#p18--make-phrasing-robustness-a-gate. EXCEPTION recorded 2026-08-07 (P24, intercity_mode oracle-side fix): easy/medium/human raised manually, not via --update-floor (which can only ratchet a set's count down and cannot express this case). `_parse_intercity` (chinatravel/agent/tpc_agent/solver_constraints.py) did not recognize the `intercity_transport_set` equality shape the HF free-prose generator actually uses, so the oracle side of clause_is_covered() silently dropped a real `intercity_mode` requirement on every query using that shape and classified its clause as `schema_gap` (uninformative) instead of `parse_gap`. Fixing that oracle-side gap correctly reclassifies those clauses -- most become covered (the NL fallback already had the right value), and the remainder (easy +2, medium +33, human +27) become newly-visible, real parse gaps ('we have chosen to fly' / 'traveling by high-speed train (G)' phrasing the NL parser does not yet catch) that were always there but invisible to this gate. See docs/tpc_phase2_roadmap.md#p24--stop-inventing-satisfiable-but-unrequested-constraints.
